resources.string: %s. Sabre 6.1 merges on a grid twice as dense as the sensor (four subpositions ±0.25 px per pixel, kernel in sensor pixels): 50 MP for a 12 MP sensor. All processing, sharpening included, runs on the 2× grid, and only at the end is the frame scaled down to the chosen size (4:3 of the sensor; “12 MP” on a 12 MP sensor = sensor size with supersampling). “2× (50 MP)” keeps the full size. Needs ≈3 GB of free memory; merging and processing take ≈×4 longer. The same setting is in the quick settings shade.
%s. Scaling down the finished frame after sharpening: Lanczos‑3 (sharpest), Bicubic (softer, no ringing), Area (averaging, no aliasing), Bilinear (fastest). In linear light.
N frames from ZSL, Bento, Shasta

4–44, default 30 (ArkCam merges about 30). Normal-exposure frames from the ZSL buffer before the press (no more than the buffer holds at the same exposure). Sabre detail shows from about 12–15 frames and keeps growing towards 30; each frame adds about 0.1 s to the merge and 25 MB of memory at 12 MP (a Quad stream merges at most the frames of «Frames in the mosaic merge»).

%s. A frame with N/8 exposure replaces the overexposed areas of the base frame (mask: threshold 0.98, dilation 4, smoothing σ=1; skipped when the clipped area is small, with holes ≥15 cells, or if the frame itself is more than 62 %% clipped). Auto: taken when the ZSL frame has clipping.

%s. Inside the overexposure mask the light comes only from the ultra-short frames. One frame: noise ×8 from the gain and the Bayer grid of a single frame. A second frame at the same exposure halves the noise in the highlights and fills R/B gaps through hand shake; the cost is one more frame after the press (~30–50 ms) and ~25 MB of memory.

%s. The check (an ultra-short frame clearly darker than the base means motion) runs for each ultra-short frame: the frame weight in the mask follows its own validity, and the base comes back only where none of them fits. Mode 2 also counts as motion an unclipped base cell that the ultra-short frame shows clearly brighter (a hand moved off a lamp). Removes the dark silhouette of a hand in a lamp when the hand is not in every frame.
Bento: skip on motion, % of mask

If more than this share of the Bento mask cells has motion (the ultra-short frame clearly darker than the base or, with check 2, clearly brighter than an unclipped base; with two frames, the better one counts), Bento is not applied, even in “Always” mode. Otherwise a moving object (a hand, a changing screen) is built from noisy scraps of ultra-short frames. Default 4; lower skips more often, 100 never. Measured: hand at a screen at night 8.1, still scenes 0–0.13, handheld by day near water 2.2.
Bento: how many times shorter than N
2–16, default 8 (ultrashort_tet_factor). Higher keeps brighter light sources in range, but the mask dilation band comes from a single high-gain frame and is noisy.
Share of overexposed pixels in the ZSL frame from which an ultra-short frame is taken. 0: any clipping.

After the press, 1–5 frames are taken with 2^EV times the exposure of N, through gain at the shutter of N, like ArkCam on the same phone (5 frames, 10 ms × gain 2.2): with no extra blur they pass the sharpness threshold and lower shadow noise. The shutter gets longer only beyond the sensor gain range (up to 1/8 s handheld). A blurred frame is dropped (threshold in “Merge”).
1–5, default 5 (as in ArkCam). Each frame adds ~33 ms after the press and ~25 MB of memory.
1–4, default 1 (×2; ArkCam by day ×1.9). Higher gives brighter shadows but more gain in each frame.

%s. Noise model of each frame for rejection, weights and the kernel SNR key. Default: SENSOR_NOISE_PROFILE from Camera2 for the ISO of each frame; “From settings” takes the profile from the “Sensor noise model” section.
Multiplier of the signal-dependent part of the frame noise profile (0.25–4, default 1).
Multiplier of the constant part of the frame noise profile, which matters in the shadows (0.25–4, default 1).
%s. vivo motion tracker for frame homographies. System: from /vendor on vivo; bundled: the same library from the APK, works on other phones too. Auto: system if present, otherwise bundled.

%s. On top of the frame homography: a shift per 16 RAW px tile (window 32, two-level Lucas–Kanade, falls back to the homography on flat, clipped and moving areas). Residual mismatch of handheld daytime frames 0.77 → 0.09 px: Sabre collects fine detail instead of blurring it. ~0.8 s per shot.

Multiplier of the colour distance between a frame and the base. Default 0.2 (0.07 in the source). Higher means stricter motion rejection, lower means more frames in the merge. At 0.07, leaves and branches in the wind shifted by 0.5–2 px were accepted and gave stepped edges (luma zipper); 0.2 on synthetic data: moving object edges +0.8 dB, moving texture +1.8 dB, 4–10 % fewer frames in the merge on still series.
Expected variance of the frame−base difference = base noise + this share of the frame noise (bilinear sampling). Default 0.5; lower is stricter.
rej = (Σ25 − 0.2) / value. Default 2. Lower spreads the rejection wider to the neighbours.
Cell rejection below this value counts as noise and does not spread to the neighbours. Default 0.15 (0 in the source, which uses a different noise domain).
As in GCam 11: where local alignment sees different motion in neighbouring tiles (a hand, foliage) and the base is textured, donor rejection is boosted ×6. Removes ghosts of moving objects.
motion_robustness_boost_variance_threshold = 25 (base variance in noise thresholds above which the boost turns on).
Range of the local flow over 3×3 tiles above which the boost turns on (GCam 11 extra_motion_robustness_motion_threshold).

%s. GCam 6.1 kernel: σ curves and SNR key 6.1, kernel covariance of each frame from its own RAW, window ±1.5 px, base kernel widening below 4 accepted frames. Auto: at night (SNR key not above the limit) and by day for handheld shots with local alignment on (daytime noise multipliers 16/4); on a still series the round 4 kernel. Off: the round 4 kernel.
Auto turns on kernel 6.1 if the 6.1 SNR key of the shot is not above this value (night: about 12, day: about 67). Default 30.
Kernel 6.1 by day: hand shake from, px
By day, Auto turns on kernel 6.1 only with local alignment and an average frame shift of at least this much (RAW px). On a still series 6.1 only adds noise. Default 2.

Multiplier of every kernel σ (across/along an edge, flat; SNR curves: GCam 6.1 with kernel 6.1, otherwise the round 4 kernels). Applies to both kernels. 1 as in Sabre; lower is sharper and noisier, higher is softer.
Noise scale for the SNR key
Variance multiplier when computing the mid-grey SNR that selects the kernel σ. Default 0.25. Round 4 kernel only: kernel 6.1 computes its own key from the frame noise model.
Share of noise variance subtracted from the structure tensor of the base greens (default 0.75). Round 4 kernel only: kernel 6.1 builds the tensor of each frame with its own noise correction.
Base kernel widening at low coverage
Accumulated donor weight below which the base frame kernel widens (Sabre 6.1: 4.0). With kernel 6.1: the number of accepted frames below which the base kernel widens ×0.3 in precision.

Where fewer donors are accepted than the kernel widening threshold (branches and leaves in the wind), R and B of the base frame are taken as merged G + the R−G (B−G) difference of real samples: removes the colour zipper along edges. The Sabre kernel is per channel, so widening σ does not cure the zipper. Default 1, 0: off (as before). Synthetic data with a single base frame: edges +5.8 dB PSNR, flat sky −0.5 dB.

The restored R (B) stays within the range of the base\'s own samples around the pixel: at a thin diagonal line the green neighbours of a sample lie on both sides of the line, and without the limit the colour would bleed along it.
Maximum scalar weight of a long frame relative to the base. Default 50.
A = ((TET/TET_base)²·read_b/read_f)^fwe. 1 without motion estimation, 0.5 with motion.
Shasta frames with weight A ≥ 30 are merged with a wider kernel: less noise in the shadows, less detail. 10 → ×1.0, 30 → ×1.414; 1.0: LUT off.
Quad 2×2 and Tetra 4×4: subframe split or native merge, frames and sharpness

For modules whose stream arrives as a mosaic (sensor mode without remosaic). Subframe split: each frame is split into normal Bayer subframes by colour block sites, and the merge assembles them on the sensor grid, like GCam QuadBayerRgbMerge. Native mosaic (default for Quad 2×2): every frame stays one frame; alignment and rejection run on its binned copy, and the merge reads each mosaic site at its own position (the Sabre Quad kernel of ArkCam v23 with our site gains, alignment and false-colour guard).

4–32, default 30 (ArkCam merges about 30). No more than the frames sent (N frames from ZSL). Each frame gives 4 (Quad) or 16 (Tetra) subframes on the split, the GPU holds 128 (Tetra: 8 frames); the native merge takes one GPU slot per frame. More frames give less noise and allow a narrower kernel; on the X7 Ultra the split takes ≈ 8 s with 24 Quad frames, ≈ 6.8 s with 16.

Multiplier of the Sabre kernel across edges and in texture for mosaic subframes (the flat-area kernel, and with it the noise, stays the same). A subframe is 2 (Quad) or 4 (Tetra) sensor pixels, so the kernel can be narrower. Default 0.6: a handheld shot on the X7 Ultra gets +14 % fine detail with the same noise in flat areas; lower is sharper, but grain shows more in dark plain areas. Subframe split only: the native merge has its own “Kernel across edges” below.

%s. Native mosaic (default for Quad 2×2 and Tetra 4×4): one GPU slot per frame; alignment and rejection run on the binned frames and the merge weights every site of its window at its true position (ArkCam\'s Sabre Quad kernel with our site gains, local alignment, rejection, Bento and false-colour guard). On the OPPO it merges 22 frames in 2–3 s, about twice as fast as the split, with +11–12 %% fine detail at the same noise on handheld shots. Subframe split: b² Bayer subframes per frame, the former default. Tetra follows “Tetra path” (native by default).

1–6, default 3: sites within r sensor pixels of the sample position (3 = a 7×7 window). Quad parity with the split: 3; ArkCam uses 2 (5×5) with its narrow kernel. Native Tetra takes twice as many sensor pixels, at most 8 (default 6 = a 13×13 window, the same reach in colour blocks).

On (default): the whole (2r+1)² square of sites around the nearest site. Off: the split\'s window (|d| ≤ r with the Sabre 6.1 window), for an exact comparison with the split. On the synthetic Quad series the full window gave 7–10 % less noise in flat areas at the same detail.

Default 0.7: all parts of the kernel narrower than the split\'s (1 = the split\'s kernel in sensor pixels). Lower is sharper and noisier. ArkCam\'s point is 0.5 with 0.5 across edges: on the test poster ArkCam\'s noise with 21 frames against its 30 and 0.96 of its detail. At night (6.1 night key) the merge keeps 1.

Multiplier of the Sabre 6.1 kernel across edges and of the base kernel in the native merge (along edges and in flat areas it stays). Default 0.6; ArkCam\'s point 0.5 (sharper, a little more false colour). Lower than 0.5 colours edges on real shots. Sabre 6.1 kernel only.

Width of the Sabre kernel of flat areas in the native merge (×; edges and texture keep theirs). Default 2.4: the noise of plain areas falls while the kernel on edges stays narrow (on the test poster ArkCam\'s kernel with 1.4 here: a quarter less wall noise for 4 % less poster detail). Lower is grainier.

%s. ArkCam stores its kernel in a texture whose range keeps it at least 0.24 px wide across edges. Default: the same range on the axes of the kernel (its direction kept); per component as ArkCam turns a narrow kernel on diagonal edges and colours them; off lets the kernel become narrower than a site (zipper, coloured edges).
Distance multiplier of the green kernel (ArkCam ks): below 1 wider, above 1 narrower. Default 1.
The same for red and blue, which have a quarter of the sites. Default 0.85 (ArkCam): 1.18× wider than green, 7 % less false colour on fine bars.

%s. ArkCam: in every frame a colour with too little kernel weight is topped up with G + (R − G) of the 3×3 colour-block means. Meant for narrow kernels and few frames; with a full series it carries colour across edges (−3…−5 dB on edges of the synthetic series).
Minimum red / blue kernel weight relative to green; below it the fill acts. Default 0.25 (ArkCam).

%s. T1 (default): the Tetra mosaic merged natively, every site at its true position with ArkCam\'s Sabre Quad kernel on 4×4 colour blocks; on the vivo X200 Ultra (10× ISZ) it merges 17 frames faster than the split merges 8, with 2–5 dB more detail, a quarter of the false colour and less noise. Subframe split: 16 Bayer subframes per frame, at most 8 frames (the former default). T2: every 2×2 sub-block of a Tetra block becomes one site of a Quad mosaic at half size, merged by the Quad pass and scaled 2×; it loses the finest Tetra detail (4–8 px).
Bento and Shasta in the merge
Weights and kernels of short and long frames
Scalar weight A of the frame in the highlights. Default 1.0.

Inside the mask the ultra-short frame is merged alone, without demosaicing: an isotropic kernel σ (px). Below 0.7 leaves gaps in R/B (green-magenta “lightning” along highlight edges), higher gives softer highlights. Default 1.0.
Bento: highlight edge colour, σ px

Inside the mask R and B are taken as G × the R/G, B/G ratios of the ultra-short frames on an isotropic kernel of this width (sensor px). With a narrow kernel R and B come from the nearest grid sample, and on a slanted clipped edge the colour changes in 2 px steps: an orange-blue dotted line. Default 2, 0: off (as before).
A long frame with sharpness below this share of the base frame sharpness is dropped. Default 0.8. Lower allows more blur.
If a long frame is brighter than the base by more than this factor, long frames are not merged. Default 32.

If at least one site in a Bayer cell of a frame is clipped, all colours of that cell of that frame go to the clipped average, not only the clipped channel: along an overexposed edge green is no longer averaged from the dark side only. Magenta fringe around lamps at night: 25 % → 9.5 %. Off: per channel, as before.

A site that, averaged over 8 normal frames, differs from its same-colour neighbours by more than this many σ (either way) gives no sample: red and blue dots at night (fixed sensor noise). The site stays if neighbours of other colours repeat it (a real point in the scene). Default 5, 0: off.
The same for single outliers (RTS) of the base frame itself, which does not go through rejection. Default 7, 0: off.
Hot pixels: only at SNR key ≤
The outlier search works only in dark areas of the frame and only in shots with a 6.1 SNR key not above this value (night): by day at ISO 100 dark texture was taken for outliers. Default 30.

An ultra-short brightness error ≥ 0.9 narrows the mask; Bento is skipped when: the clipped share is small → a hole ≥ 15 cells → the ultra-short frame is more than 62 % clipped. Off: the round 4 checks.
Lens colour fringing: CA_correct from RawTherapee

%s. RawTherapee CA_correct algorithm: green is estimated at the R and B sites, the shift of the red and blue grids relative to green is measured in 128 px tiles, the field is smoothed with a polynomial, and R / B are corrected through the colour difference with G (green samples stay unchanged). “Estimate from the base frame”: the base frame field shifts R / B of the finished merge (instead of the old radial correction). “Correct every frame (GPU)”: every frame of the series is corrected on the GPU before alignment and merging. Off: as before.
Shifts are measured on the shot (like Auto in RawTherapee). Off: manual radial correction “Red” / “Blue”.

How many times to measure the residual and correct again (RawTherapee: 2). Each pass is a new measurement and correction; on synthetic data with known CA the second pass lowers the red error at the frame edges from 66 to 53 codes, the third to 50.
Manual correction without auto detect: radial shift of red at the frame edge (from the sensor centre), like “Red” in RawTherapee. Default 0.

The geometric R / B correction can slightly change the overall colour of an area: the before / after ratio is smoothed (σ 60 px) and put back, and the fringe stays corrected (Avoid color shift in RawTherapee).
GCam / Hybrid, SNR, Luma and Chroma tables

One switch for all Hybrid denoisers. Off: no denoising after the merge (GCam or NLM, dot removal), no Bento denoising in the highlights and no chroma denoising of lifted shadows; only the frame merge itself remains.

%s. GCam / Hybrid: the GCam finishing denoiser, as in ArkCam (luma and chroma pyramids, strength by frame SNR; settings in the section below). NLM: the old Hybrid denoiser; the two strengths below apply only to it.
Removes single dark/bright pixels on smooth areas. On sea or sky in a window (Bento) it can erase small distant objects; turn it off then.
Bento: denoise boost limit in highlights

How many times stronger the denoiser cleans areas merged from a single ultra-short frame (by the merge\'s effective frame map). 3 as before; 8–12 is closer to the real noise of a frame with gain ×8…16 (GCam does not model this noise at all).
NLM engine only. Strength of the NLM luma denoiser on the merged frame (0: off). Default 0.6; the noise level is measured on the frame itself.
NLM engine only. Strength of the bilateral chroma denoiser and colour blotch suppression (0: off). Default 1.0.
Manual SNR, multiplier, ρs and ρr, strength map

Table point by the SNR of the finishing input (like “Finish input frame SNR” in GCam). 0: auto, SNR = 0.18 / exposure gain over the noise of the merged frame. For debugging: 5 night (SabreLow), 7.8 ArkCam night on vivo, 10, 20, 40.
0.25–8, default 1. Higher treats the shot as cleaner (weaker chroma denoising, luma revert below 1).
How many times the noise model that ArkCam passes to GCam is noisier than the real one in the photon part (vivo: 1.2). Goes into the filter thresholds and the SNR.
The same for the constant part (shadows; vivo: 5–7, default 6). Higher gives stronger smoothing in the shadows and a lower SNR.

%s. Map of the merge\'s effective frames: areas from a single frame (Bento ×k at lamps) are cleaned harder, up to the limit “Bento: denoise boost limit in highlights”. Uniform: as in ArkCam (not proven).
0–4, default 1: all luma strength values (pref_luma_denoise_multiplier). 0: luma is left alone.
0–4, default 1: all chroma strength values (with the lower limit). 0: colour is left alone.
0–4, default 1 (spatial strength): the share of the uncleaned luma level.

0–9, default 9 as in ArkCam: below SNR 10 the removed fine grain comes back with a gain of up to ×9 (F16 without a limit). 1: an honest denoiser without revert; 2: the old safeguard (less “sand” at night).

0–1, default 0 as in ArkCam: luma bands b2–b4 (period 4–32 px) are left alone and texture stays. Higher: the share of the stock GCam strength/revert against large blotches (0.5 is the old value, it washes out texture).
0–5, default 0: the pure ArkCam table. Higher: a lower limit of colour strength on bands b0–b2 (2.75 = ArkCam at SNR 7.8; the old value), smoother colour at high SNR.

0–1, default 0. Colour finer than a sensor pixel on the 2× grid (mostly colour noise, which the pyramid does not see): 0 takes the 2× colour cleaned from the sensor scale, as at 1×; 1 keeps all of it.
Fade colour in the darkest areas
The colour of the darkest pixels (below ~0.003) goes neutral: it is a black level error, not noise. GCam does not do this.
Luma Denoise, points t1–t5: strength, revert, outlier per band b0–b4. ArkCam 2.85 values; linear in SNR between points.
L1B…L4B, L5A; 0–1 (×16 = share of strict weights). ArkCam: 0.6,0.4,0.2447,0.2383,0.3473.
L1B…L4B, L5A; 0–1 (×16 = share of strict weights). ArkCam: 1,1,1,0.3731,0.4647.
L1B…L4B, L5A; 0–1 (×16 = share of strict weights). ArkCam: 0.7,0.4,0.322,0.508,0.582.
L1B…L4B, L5A; 0–1 (×16 = share of strict weights). ArkCam: 0.6,0.6,0.4725,0.363,0.0777.
L1B…L4B, L5A; 0–1 (×16 = share of strict weights). ArkCam: 1,1,1,0.363,0.0777.
Chroma Denoise, points t1–t4: strength and outlier per band b0–b4. ArkCam 2.85 values.
L2…L5 (b0 is 0); integers 0–16 (sum of spatial weights). ArkCam: 0,5,5,4,4.
L2…L5 (b0 is 0); integers 0–16 (sum of spatial weights). ArkCam: 0,5,5,4,4.
L2…L5 (b0 is 0); integers 0–16 (sum of spatial weights). ArkCam: 0,5,5,4,4.
L2…L5 (b0 is 0); integers 0–16 (sum of spatial weights). ArkCam: 0,5,5,4,4.
Sharpening, tone mapping, vibrance: shared by Hybrid and SCAM HDR

%s. ARK: ArkCam sharpening before the tone (needs the ARK tone; settings: “ARK tone” → “ARK sharpening”); without the ARK tone RawTherapee works instead. RawTherapee: Unsharp Mask, RL deconvolution and microcontrast with the “Sharpening and detail” settings (radii are rescaled on the 2× grid); SCAM: a halo-free luma unsharp mask that weakens by itself on noisy frames.

Works when “Hybrid sharpening” = ARK. As in ArkCam 2.85: bilateral lift, local contrast and two Richardson–Lucy stages on luma before the tone; the detail enters as the delta ∛S − ∛reference. Defaults: ArkCam X8U, main camera.
Multiplier of the ArkCam detail delta (∛S(guide) − ∛reference) added after the tone. 1 as in ArkCam.

1 as in ArkCam: the guide at the G_CLEAN scale (without the ae exposure); halo and highlight thresholds are computed on it. 0: after the ae exposure; brighter in dark scenes, strong edges fade earlier.
0: auto, 1 on the 12 MP grid, 2 on the 50 MP grid (radii ×2, so that a shot scaled down to 12 MP is sharpened as in ArkCam).
RawTherapee on top of ARK sharpening (weaker in lifted shadows). ArkCam does not have it.

RawTherapee / SCAM sharpening after the tone (RawTherapee and SCAM modes or “Extra sharpening after the tone”) gets weaker where the fusion lifted the shadows: weight = lift^(−x). 0: the same sharpening everywhere; 0.5: default (lift ×4 → sharpening ×0.5).
0–2, default 1. Multiplier of the RawTherapee Unsharp Mask and microcontrast strength for Hybrid shots only; the RawTherapee settings themselves do not change.
Gaussian σ, px on the 12 MP grid. ArkCam: 0.5.
In 1/255 of brightness: a difference below the threshold is not boosted. ArkCam: 50 (USM barely acts).
Lift of fine detail: brightness minus its bilateral blur. ArkCam: 1.
Brightness σ in hundredths: a larger difference is an edge and is not blurred. ArkCam: 10.
Guided filter, px on the 12 MP grid. 0: off. ArkCam: 8.
Brightness minus the guided filter, × value. ArkCam: 0.25.
Amplitude in 1/255, stronger in the midtones. ArkCam: 0.
Three stages and halo suppression. ArkCam: Airy r 1 ×3, stage 2 off, Gaussian 0.5 ×3.
%: the RL overshoot is limited to the local min/max. ArkCam: 100.
Overshoot allowance on weak edges. ArkCam: 0.15.
3×3 range from which RL fades out on strong edges. ArkCam: 0.4.
px on the 12 MP grid; 0: stage off. ArkCam: 1.
px on the 12 MP grid (σ for Gaussian); 0: stage off. ArkCam: 0.5.
%: sharpening fades below 0.2 × value of the guide brightness. ArkCam: 0.
%: sharpening fades from 1 − 0.2 × value towards white. ArkCam: 100 (from 0.8).
%: on strong edges (3×3 range from 0.15 to 0.40) the added detail fades and the overshoot is limited to the local min/max. ArkCam: 100.
AE, Smart HDR, layer weights, curves
Target geometric mean brightness after AE (by day; at night the night factor lowers the target). ArkCam 2.85: 0.15.
Face weight in metering and in highlight protection (Hybrid does not receive faces yet). ArkCam: 0.7.
Lower bound of the AE multiplier. ArkCam: 0.5.
Upper bound of the AE multiplier. ArkCam 2.85: 5.
AE is limited when the 99.5th percentile after AE is above the threshold. ArkCam 2.85: 2.
0: AE fully yields to highlight protection, 1: protection off. ArkCam: 0.33.
AE to the power x when x ≠ 1. ArkCam: 1.

Above this ISO (of the reference frame, that is the preview) the AE target smoothly drops to 0.29× at the sensor\'s maximum analog ISO, and the fusion does not lift the shadows (night factor). ArkCam: 100.

One multiplier of the linear input before the statistics (2^EV): brings it to the G_CLEAN scale (Google ds_linear_rgb) that ArkCam AE works on. 0 by default: the Hybrid input (sensor white = 1) is already at this scale (measured: G_CLEAN = RAW × 0.85–0.96).
Level after AE above which the fusion darkens the highlights (highlight strength). ArkCam: 0.8.
Lower gives a stronger shadow lift by the fusion. ArkCam 2.85: 15.
Scenes with a brightness spread below the threshold get extra AgX contrast. ArkCam 2.85: 10.
Multiplier of the fusion highlight strength. ArkCam: 1.
Added to the AgX slope for flat scenes. ArkCam 2.85: 0.5.
Ceiling of the shadow lift: exposures ×2^S and ×2^2S. ArkCam 2.85: 2.
Ceiling of the highlight darkening: exposure ×2^(−1.5H). ArkCam 2.85: 2.
A pure 1/γ power (not the piecewise sRGB). ArkCam: 2.2.
Film toe: display brightness below 0.15 is pulled towards black. ArkCam: 0.1.
0: Default, 1: Punchy, 2: Soft, 3: Golden (warm highlights, no hue hold), 4: Custom (the parameters below). ArkCam 2.85: 4.
ArkCam 2.85: 2.7 (for flat scenes plus the Smart HDR contrast strength).
OPPO Find X7 Ultra only: our ISP colour matrix is more saturated than the DNG matrices ArkCam renders with (≈1.6×). AgX saturation multiplier for such shots; 0.6 as in ArkCam, 1: no compensation.
ACES toe in the fusion brightness and in the inverse transform. ArkCam 2.85: 0.05.
OKLab lightness around 0.40, without a spatial part. ArkCam: 1.1.
Display brightness of a layer to which the fusion gives the most weight. ArkCam 2.85: 0.6.
Width of the Gaussian layer weights. ArkCam 2.85: 0.25.
At half the sensor size; the box filter works with half the radius on a map scaled down by two. ArkCam: 32.
eps = value / 1000. Higher makes the fusion map smoother and more global, lower makes it more precise at edges. ArkCam: 1 (eps 0.001).

Without ARK sharpening: strength of the fine detail of the full-size merge added after the tone (not boosted in lifted shadows, half as strong towards white). 1 matches the ArkCam detail. Default 2: on Oppo at night +22 % fine detail over ArkCam with lower luma noise than ArkCam.
ArkCam has no midtone frequency lift, so “Texture” is off with the ARK tone. On: SCAMERA local contrast with the strength from the “Texture” slider in the “Tone” section.

Clip level of each channel before white balance; a clipped channel is raised by the colour of the surrounding light (a white lamp stays white, no magenta), fully clipped areas smoothly go to neutral white, a single coloured channel (neon, laser) is left alone. Also works with Bento (clip flags from the worker). Default 100, 0: off.
Highlights: trust threshold for surrounding colour
How coloured the light around a clip may be for recovery to take its colour: further from neutral it smoothly goes to white (a white lamp on a red wall stays white). Default 0.35.

0–1, default 0.85. At a clip boundary (1–2 px) the colours come from different sides of a sharp edge: a dotted red-blue fringe along the edges of lamps and paper. Keeps the brightness and takes the colour of the local light, like the ArkCam defringe. 0: off.

Smooths the orange-blue dotted line along a bright slanted edge at a clipped highlight (frames, window sills): on the edge the merge alternates colour from clipped and unclipped samples. Only at near-white clipped highlights; coloured light sources are left alone. 0: off, 1: default.
A 5×5 cross-bilateral filter for pixels brighter than 0.95 (the short Bento frame) before the fusion. ArkCam: 1.
Path to white for bright coloured light
Saturated bright light (LED, neon, lamps) at the curve shoulder goes to white instead of freezing at one colour. 0: off
Where detail darkens an edge, colour drops together with brightness: no magenta/green line on the dark side of contrasty edges. 0 as in ArkCam (colour does not change), 1: default.
Suppresses fine detail below the threshold (noise of flat areas). ArkCam 2.85: 0.
Desaturates pixels that the fusion lifted more than 4 times. ArkCam 2.85: 0.
Saturated colours are left alone. ArkCam 2.85: 0.
Blue hues, saturated ones protected. ArkCam 2.85: 0.40.
Green hues, saturated ones protected. ArkCam 2.85: 0.20.
After a Hybrid shot a ZIP with intermediate images and numeric data is saved to Download/SCAMERA. Slows processing down and takes space.

Normal-exposure frames from the ZSL buffer. 4 as in stock. More: the extra frames are aligned to the reference and averaged into the 4 N slots of the model and into the reference Luma/Chroma merge: less noise, more information. No more than the buffer holds at the same exposure; ~25 MB of memory and a little time per frame.

0–2 EV, default 1.1; 0 = stock plan. The L frame is longer than stock: our preview is exposed about 1.1 EV darker than stock, so the shadows get less signal. The shutter is extended up to 1/8 s (never shorter than stock), the rest comes from gain. Handheld blur and model artefacts at transitions are possible.

%s. Stock vivo motion tracker for aligning SCAM HDR frames. System: from /vendor on vivo; bundled: the same library from the APK with stubs for the vivo dependencies, works on other phones too. Auto: system if present, otherwise bundled.

L is not taken after the press: it is built from all ZSL N frames (more light and less noise than a single 1/8 s L). After the press only the short S and ES are taken, and the shutter is free about 0.25 s sooner.

%s. Stock vivo AE: the exact stock calculation through a root observer (vivo X200 Ultra only, needs the Root access switch). SCAMERA: no root, for any device: N by the preview exposure (ZSL), L/S/ES by the steps below.
0–3, default 1 (as in stock). The L boost below is added on top.
2–9, default 6; always at least 1 EV below S.
By the share of overexposed pixels in the last ZSL frame: with no overexposure S/ES are milder (−2/−4 EV, less noise), with heavy overexposure ES goes deeper (−7 EV).

Inside SCAM HDR. Luma denoise strength. 0: no denoising (all the detail and grain of the frame merge); 1: as the model was trained. In between only what is at the noise level is removed: texture and edges well above the noise stay (threshold by noise variance, as in HDR+). Usually 0.3–0.5 for day, 0.6–0.9 for night. 1–2: extra luma smoothing on top of the model.

Inside SCAM HDR. Chroma denoise strength. 0: merge colour without denoising; 1: as the model was trained; in between only colour blotches at the noise level are suppressed and real colour detail stays. 1–2: extra colour smoothing on top of the model, guided by luma.
1–4 pixels, for strength above 1. Higher is softer but loses fine detail.
1–12 pixels, for strength above 1. Higher removes large colour blotches more strongly.
A wide edge-aware chroma denoiser over the whole frame: removes large colour blotches in the shadows (walls, sky) and keeps luma and fine colour. 0: off, 1: default, 2: stronger.
Luma denoising after SCAM HDR by the noise model (as in GCam: fine even grain instead of blotches and “wax”; edges and texture stay). 0: off, 0.6: default (grain as in Hybrid), 1: twice as clean.
Single dark or bright dots on flat areas (defective pixel groups of the sensor that the merge keeps) go back to the level of their surroundings. Edges and texture are not touched.

0.25–4; original 1. Changes the noise variance in the VST before the neural network and in the inverse transform. An experimental setting of the SCAM HDR adapter, not an RGB filter. Zero is not supported; the model\'s built-in noise reduction is not turned off.
Changes the signal-dependent part of the noise profile before SCAM HDR. 1: original; an experimental control of the model input, with no filter on top of the result.
Changes the constant part of the noise profile before SCAM HDR, which matters most in the shadows. 1: original. This is not a separate control of luma or colour.
0.55–2.2; original 1.1 from the Vivo profile. Changes the scale of the model input and of the inverse VST. The quality of changed values needs checking on shots.

%s. For modules with ISZ (2× Quad, 4× Tetra): RAW arrives as a mosaic, and SCAM HDR first turns it into a normal Bayer. Off: as before, a normal Bayer is needed. The block size comes from the module\'s sensor mode. The neural network and Multi-frame Remosaic build one frame from the N frames (needs 6+ N for Tetra, 4+ for Quad; the GPU remosaics the other S/ES/L frames); on an error, a fallback GPU remosaic of all frames. Sabre on raw samples: the merge kernel takes donor samples straight from the mosaic (up to 16 N frames), while the network and alignment use the remosaic; needs Luma and Chroma not equal to 1 (they turn on the Sabre merge).
Works on the telephoto lens in 4× ISZ mode, Tetra 4×4. Settings apply to the next shot. For the old result: x2, original size, multipliers 1, auto by ISO off, texture 0.

The CPU aligns frames and prepares the input in parallel with the neural network on the NPU. The GPU restores detail and blends luma/chroma. The mode is on automatically; if the GPU fails, the CPU runs its stages.
x1 is an experimental model: it had colour errors in tests. The chosen model and profile are checked before shooting. Both options use six frames.
1: original HP9 profile. Changes the noise power estimate before the network. Does not change ISO; the effect on quality needs checking.
Extra multiplier of the part that grows with the signal. Multiplied by the overall one; 1: original value.
Extra multiplier of the constant part of the profile, noticeable in the shadows. Multiplied by the overall one; 1: original value.
100: luma from the network; 0: plain reconstruction of the first RAW. Lower keeps more of the original texture and noise.
100: colour from the network; 0: colour of the plain reconstruction. This blends the results after the network.
Lowers the network\'s share of luma on detail above the expected noise. Chroma keeps the chosen strength. 0: off; grain and grid may come back.

Lossless JPEG inside DNG: the file is about 40 % smaller, the data is bit-identical. Processing a shot in RAW and RAW+JPEG modes takes ~0.2 s (12 MP) to ~0.8 s (50 MP) longer. LibRaw / RawTherapee read it; check Lightroom, darktable and your gallery before relying on it.

%s. The STATISTICS_LENS_SHADING_CORRECTION_MAP map (up to ×5 in the corners). Auto: always apply, as before (the HAL flag SENSOR_INFO_LENS_SHADING_APPLIED is unreliable: vivo reports it, but without the map the RAW is wrong). “Do not apply”: for cameras whose RAW is already corrected in the ISP; otherwise the edges get brighter and their black level rises.

If dark areas in the RAW itself are below the black level the HAL reports, black is lowered to the real floor of the frame (from the shortest frame of the series). Fixes green shadows on the OPPO Find X8 Ultra: RAW_SENSOR reports 64, but the data starts at ~60. Only lowers black; a manual “Black level” in “Sensor settings per module” takes priority.

%s. Auto: RAW_SENSOR (16-bit container) if the camera offers it, otherwise RAW10, then RAW12. Packed RAW10/RAW12 are unpacked to 16 bits when copied and in the RAW viewfinder; black and white levels come from the camera characteristics, and the merge does not depend on the bit depth. RAW10 by default on the OPPO Find X8 Ultra.

For OPPO / OnePlus and generic Android: unlock hidden modules
Off: the camera sees the SCAMERA package itself and no hook is installed. Changes apply the next time the camera opens; the camera list updates after the app restarts.

OnePlus/OPPO: OplusCameraManager.saveOpPackageName (unlocks hidden cameras and Oplus vendor modes). Generic Android: replaces the package in the CameraManager context, does not bypass the UID check in CameraService. BinderHook: rewrites the package name directly in ICameraService transactions (experimental). Empty field: the app\'s own package. Example: com.android.camera on vivo, com.oplus.camera on OPPO.

JPEG opens everywhere and is the only format with Ultra HDR. HEIC: about half the size at the same look; Android 9+, iPhone, and Windows / macOS with the codec open it. WebP: smaller than JPEG; browsers and most apps open it, not every gallery; up to 16383 px per side, a larger photo is saved as JPEG. RAW keeps the sensor data as DNG; RAW + a format saves both.
Default 90. Lower gives a smaller file; fine detail goes sooner. Without an HEVC encoder on the phone the photo is saved as JPEG.
Default 90. Lower gives a smaller file; fine detail goes sooner.
Exact pixels: files several times larger than lossy WebP and slower to save. Quality is not used.
A JPEG copy next to the HEIC / WebP photo for apps that cannot open them. With Ultra HDR on, this JPEG carries it.

Faces are framed on the viewfinder and steer autofocus and exposure (manual focus, manual exposure and a tap focus take precedence). Camera modes are used only where the lens offers them; Software reads the viewfinder image.
Locks focus and exposure onto a subject and follows it across the frame. When it is lost, continuous autofocus takes over again. Tapping elsewhere returns to the tap focus.
